<reason>PRO won the central circularity and staging clash. CON demanded resistance, food-web and proven recall before any outdoor step, but PRO showed that knowledge only comes from real outdoor observation, making the demand the impossible-certainty veto in disguise. CON's admission that non-driving/split outdoor work is acceptable let PRO reframe the debate as conceded staged trials vs pace, which CON's bicycle-vs-truck reply never fully escaped, leaving certain malaria deaths to outweigh hypothetical phase-gated border harm.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's Q2/Rebuttal-2 concession trap: confinable split-drive trials are acceptable outdoor gene-drive-component work, so only pace to self-sustaining stages remains, gated by evidence — turning CON's achievable-caution claim into a permanent veto.</best_rebuttal>
